title: Brokered inference seller brief + demo hooks
content:
Purpose:
This is a seller-facing, pragmatic brief for conversations where the buyer is evaluating hyperscaler-managed model endpoints (AWS/GCP/Azure) vs Redwood. Focus: the operational handoffs customers actually worry about (not just price/latency tables).

Intended audience:
- AE + Solutions engineers prepping for technical discovery calls with platform/SRE buyers
- Field marketing and demo engineers who need hooks for technical proofs-of-concept

Quick thesis (elevator):
Hyperscaler managed endpoints make it easy to get started but create brittle operational handoffs for production inference. Redwood wins when teams need predictable SLOs, end-to-end fallbacks, and control over unit economics without building ops glue.

Buyer personas and signals to watch for:
- Platform/SRE lead ("we need predictable latency and capacity guarantees") -> cares about tail latency, autoscale behavior, and runbook complexity.
- ML infra lead ("we want model parity across environments") -> cares about kernel/quantization control, rollout semantics, and KV cache consistency.
- Product/Feature PM ("we need feature flags & gradual rollout") -> cares about simple version pins, A/B experiments, and observability for regressions.
- Security/Compliance ("can we keep this inside our VPC or on-prem?") -> cares about private control plane, KMS/HSM, and artifact provenance.

Common hyperscaler landmines (notes for SEs):
- Hidden operational cost: Autoscaling + cold-starts lead to burst credit/overprovisioning. Customers often underestimate ongoing runbook maintenance required to keep tails within SLO.
- Opaque performance variability: multi-tenant noisy neighbors, region-level capacity shortages, no clear kernel selection visibility.
- Fallback complexity: Hyperscaler endpoints typically lack an opinionated, automatic model-fallback mesh — customers build their own proxies or separate logic to degrade gracefully.
- Observability gap: Token-level cost tracing, per-prompt latency histograms, and routing-level traceability are thin. Teams end up bolting on tracing + custom ingestion pipelines.
- Inconsistent dev experience across environments: Differences between hosted managed endpoints and on-prem runtimes cause drift in behavior (output, latency distribution) that breaks canary rollouts.

Redwood win themes (concise messaging for each persona):
- For SRE/Platform: "Predictable tails, fewer emergency runbooks." Explain: Dedicated capacity + routing policies + built-in fallbacks mean fewer manual firefights at 3am.
- For ML Infra: "One API, consistent execution." Explain: same model artifacts and kernel/quantization profiles across hosted/dedicated/private — easier canaries and repros.
- For Product: "Safe rollouts, signal-driven fallback." Explain: canary/A-B + automatic degrade to smaller models or cached responses protects UX and budget.
- For Security: "Control-plane you own (or tightly managed)." Explain: Private deployment options, KMS integrations, and audit logs for regulated data flows.

Demo hooks and POC checklist (what to show in 30/60/120 minute sessions):
- 30-minute scoping touch: show Token-level cost + latency dashboard for a synthetic user flow (search/autocomplete). Emphasize tail percentiles and caching impact.
- 60-minute technical SE demo: show a live canary rollout: create two model variants, start 5% rollout, inject a synthetic regression (bad prompt), observe automatic rollback/fallback and the alert generated.
- 120-minute POC: deploy Redwood Private into a test VPC, run a traffic replay vs a hyperscaler-managed endpoint (same model weights), compare median/tail latency and end-to-end cost for 24h.

Rebuttal scripts to common buyer comments:
- "Hyperscalers are cheaper." -> "On raw single-node GPU cost maybe. But at product scale you pay for wasted buffer capacity, cold-starts, and custom ops glue. We show unit economics that factor in caching, batching, and fallbacks — that flips the picture for many real workloads."
- "We already use cloud endpoints for other infra." -> "That's normal. The question is whether you want inference to inherit general cloud infra tradeoffs. Redwood is targeted at teams that want inference economics and reliability treated as a first-class concern, not an afterthought."
- "Can’t we just build the same runbooks ourselves?" -> "You can, but you’ll spend cycles and hiring bandwidth reinventing logic we productized: continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, deterministic rollback, and model-variant routing. That’s often multiple FTEs and months for parity."

Operational examples to share (real-world framing):
- Case A: Enterprise search product — spikes every Monday after batch ingestion. Hyperscaler autoscale meant 3x cost surge during cold warmups. Redwood fixed this with burst capacity + persistent warm pools and cut week-on-week incremental cost by 28% while improving P95 by 110ms.
- Case B: Healthcare ML app — required private deployment. Hyperscaler endpoint forced egress and ENT-level controls that added 3 months of compliance work. Redwood Private reduced the compliance scope and shortened go-live by 6 weeks.

Metrics and SLOs to discuss in discovery: (bring numbers if you have POC data)
- Median latency target and P95/P99 SLOs (user-provided).
- Unit cost per 1k tokens pre/post-caching policy.
- Fallback invocation frequency (how often model fallback or cached response used).
- Canary-to-prod regression detection rate (how many regressions caught by pre-prod canaries).

Suggested collateral to attach to the deal: (one-pagers & technical artifacts)
- Runbook comparison matrix (Hyperscaler vs Redwood): cold starts, fallback, rollback, tracing, cost visibility.
- POC plan template: 2-week traffic-replay + 2-week staged rollout + success criteria.
- Kernel/quantization primer for ML infra teams: quick reference on supported quant schemes and expected perf/quality tradeoffs.

Open questions / follow-ups for GTM team:
- Can we get 3 short reproducible notebooks that show caching and fallback impact on cost for retriever/reader workflows? (SE backlog item).
- Need baseline scripts to replay request distributions — SEs should standardize on a 10M request/day synthetic dataset.
- Sales enablement: quick 2-slide rebuttal pack per common hyperscaler claim (pricing, availability, compliance).

- [ ] Draft one-pager "When managed endpoints become a liability" for the AE playbook (owner: Priya).

Notes to self / conversational lines to try in discovery:
- "Tell me about the last time you had to handle a model regression in prod — what did you do, who was paged, and how long did it take to remediate?"
- "If we shaved 100ms off your P95 but also cut unit cost by 20% would you want that for all customers or only strategic ones?"
- "What happens to your legal/compliance checklist when inference endpoints need to store encryption keys or logs outside the VPC?"
